verifications.note: Judged adversarially on the same frozen candidate sha256:55a411ae9f4e87473478988f3d9909752a934a547ba40acc1479f2b2bc3a24ce (source 660f40c, re-verified on a complete clone at the start and end of this run). The defect is real and stays as described in round 2: migration 0062 seeds the five scoring_weight elements with sourceLabelEn + labelAr and no labelEn, and apps/web/src/pages/studio/api.ts elementLabel() reads only labelEn/labelAr, so on the English page the Studio Elements table falls back to the Arabic labels. Fresh code inspection in my clone (f120-f121-code-inspection.log) shows how far it reaches. elementLabel is used ONLY by apps/web/src/pages/studio/ElementsSection.tsx, the administrator's Elements table. The scoring-defaults editor names criteria through i18n studio.criterion.* (English 'Strategic fit' and the others). Every transformation-facing screen (WeightSets, Scorecard, Rankings) names them through prioritization.criterion.<code>, and my round-2 screenshot of the same candidate (screens/en/dom-p3-after-prioritization.png) shows 'Strategic fit: 30% ... Time-to-value: 15%' in English. No server scoring, ranking, gate-facts or publish code reads any of these label attributes (grep exit 1). The stable key and B0076 sit beside each label, so the row is identifiable. No weight value, calculation, pin, review, publish refusal, authorization or approval is affected, and the Arabic page is correct. No DG5 acceptance text names this table's label language: REQ-PB-093's A06/A07 clauses (30/20/20/15/15 in the UI, new transformations only, 95 % refused) passed in my round-2 runs on this candidate (DOM-R2-08). It is therefore Low, non-mandatory, presentation only, and admin-only. It is accepted as an observation for DG5, NOT closed as fixed. DG6 follow-up (owner frontend-ux-engineer): make elementLabel use sourceLabelEn in English when there is no labelEn, or seed labelEn through a new migration (never edit 0062). Prefill 'Label (English)' in the Edit dialog the same way. Add a component test that the English Elements table shows 'Strategic fit' for strategic_fit. While there, align studio.criterion.time_to_value ('Time to value') with B0076's 'Time-to-value', which prioritization.json already uses (cosmetic, same page family).

Judged adversarially on the same frozen candidate sha256:55a411ae9f4e87473478988f3d9909752a934a547ba40acc1479f2b2bc3a24ce (source 660f40c, complete clone verified at the start and end). Both halves are confirmed and explained by the code (f120-f121-code-inspection.log). (1) The Elements table's 'Change in this version' column renders studio.elements.overridden ('Changed' / 'معدّل') whenever the config element is 'overridden'. In config-resolver.ts that flag means the version holds its own row for the element, not that the value differs from the base version. The scoring-defaults editor sends the full weight set, so every weight gets an own row, and all five read 'Changed'. The column label is therefore misleading. (2) displayValue() in studio/api.ts prints non-scalar values (a rubric's levels array) as JSON.stringify, which shows raw JSON in the diff. Why it is not blocking: the side-by-side 'Differences from the base version' is computed from resolved values (diff.ts) and is correct. In my round-2 screenshots of this candidate it lists only strategic_fit 25.00 -> 30.00, financial_value 25.00 -> 20.00 and the feasibility rubric, whose changed descriptor text is legible inside the JSON. The Compatibility check lists the same three elements. A Studio reviewer therefore has an accurate, complete change list, and the misleading column cannot hide or invent a change in a way that changes what gets published. REQ-S06-007's acceptance (publish without review refused, published version 409, 'the diff lists the added field') and REQ-S06-008/REQ-PB-093 passed in my round-2 runs on this candidate (DOM-R2-03, DOM-R2-05, DOM-R2-08). No data, calculation, pin, immutability, authorization or approval effect. It is Low, non-mandatory and presentation only. It is accepted as an observation for DG5, NOT closed as fixed. DG6 follow-up (owner frontend-ux-engineer, with backend-workflow-engineer if the API must expose it): make the column show 'Changed' only when the resolved value differs from the base version (or relabel the flag, e.g. 'Set in this version'). Render rubric levels in the diff as readable per-score before/after descriptors in both languages, never raw JSON. Add tests for both (en and ar).
